notes: The registered C row is POS_DEAD with no level minimum; the focused test pins this command-surface gate (R2/R5e).
The shared POS_DEAD dispatcher rejection is already proven by the purge gate boundary (R5b/R5c).
A low-level mortal in an unsafe room receives C's exact REALLYQUIT block plus the level-five RECALL hint and remains connected (R1/R2/R5e).
The do_quit handler does not parse its argument; trailing words do not alter the unsafe-room refusal (R1/R2/R5e).
A forced mortal in temple 8004 reaches the successful logout path and receives C's exact goodbye before extraction (R1/R3/R5e).
A visible quitter emits the canonical has-left room act to the observer while the actor receives only the goodbye (R1/R3/R5e).
Both temple vnums are safe rooms and their successful rent save retains equipped items (R1/R4/R5e).
Home-room safety is conditional: 18201 requires hometown 2, while 21202 and 21258 require hometown 3 (R1/R5e).
The default branch accepts an owned house as a safe logout room and preserves equipment through save (R1/R4/R5e).
POS_FIGHTING wins before safe-room/logout handling and emits C's exact refusal (R1/R2/R5e).
POS_INCAP and below emit the death line and call die(ch), without proceeding to descriptor logout (R1/R4/R5e).
The successful visible path sends one room leave act and does not duplicate it during cleanup (R1/R3/R5e).
A successful quit turns off an active infobar before extraction (R1/R4/R5e).
Successful quit calls the shared unmount helper; rider/mount pair cleanup is owned by the dismount depth manifest (R4/R5b/R5c).
The IS_NPC or missing-descriptor early return is unreachable from a player descriptor's top-level command row; it belongs to lifecycle/runtime teardown rather than this command surface (R4/R5e).

A successful quit sends the goodbye, and the next heartbeat's extraction returns the same connection to the menu (extract_char, handler.c:1172-1174); the port now queues the extraction instead of closing the connection, and choice 1 re-enters. DP-1312 (R1/R2).

A legal quit rents: unrentable objects are destroyed, the rest leave with the character and come back on re-entry (Crash_rentsave, Crash_extract_objs, Crash_load). The earlier 'kit on the floor' was a harness artifact: the oracle lib had no plrobjs/ directory, so C's rent file failed to open; the harness now creates C's player-file trees (R1).

A quit outside a safe room rents nothing, so extract_char drops everything worn and carried where the character stood, in C's order (carried list from its head, then worn slots), for anyone to take. The port used to destroy it all (R1).

After a rent and re-entry C lists the newbie backpack at 13 pts with its bread and water skin inside. The port listed it at 1 pt because the database save wrote only top-level objects, never container contents; the weight was the symptom (DP-1324). pkg/db/convert.go now saves each container's contents after it and rebuilds the tree on load.
On the same connection, menu choice 1 after a legal quit re-enters with the rented objects back (C's Crash_load; the port reloads the character from its store) (R1/R2).
